items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. As a Talent Acquisition Operations Associate, reporting to the Sr. Manager, Talent Acquisition and Operations, you will help run the operations behind Payward’s global hiring engine. You will support the systems, processes, and coordination that keep hiring moving at pace, from interview operations and executive hiring to pre-boarding, background checks, and new hire setup in Workday. This role extends well beyond scheduling. It requires a strategic view of how a fast-growing, global company hires, along with precision, discretion, and sound judgment. You will partner closely with recruiters, hiring managers, and executive assistants to support scheduling, anticipate bottlenecks, and keep stakeholders aligned at every stage. You will work heavily in our recruiting tools, keeping candidate and hiring data accurate and up to date across regions. This is a 6-month fixed-term position supporting US timezones. The opportunity - Own interview operations end to end, partnering with recruiters, hiring managers, and candidates across regions and time zones to deliver a seamless candidate experience - Support global executive and non-executive hiring operations, including scheduling and rescheduling, tracking and candidate communications - Partner with executive assistants across regions to coordinate calendars and keep hiring timelines on track - Own pre-boarding for new hires worldwide, including country-specific background check requirements and communications, tracking progress, resolving issues, and flagging risks to start dates early - Create and maintain accurate candidate and hiring records in Ashby and Workday, and ensure new hire data is complete and timely for hires in every region - Partner with onboarding, recruiting, and hiring managers to create a seamless transition from offer acceptance to day one - Apply our hiring policies accurately and consistently across regions, flagging exceptions and escalating early What you bring - 4+ years in recruiting coordination, talent acquisition operations, HR operations, or a similar role, ideally in a high-growth, global environment spanning NORAM, EMEA, LATAM, APAC and MENA - Hands-on experience with Workday or a comparable HRIS, and familiarity with applicant tracking systems (Ashby a plus) - Experience supporting pre-boarding and onboarding, including coordinating background checks, tracking progress, resolving issues, and flagging risks to start dates early - Working knowledge of background check processes and requirements across multiple countries and regions - Comfort coordinating across time zones, with the ability to manage complex, high-volume calendars and logistics with exceptional precision and no missed details - Exceptional judgment and discretion in handling confidential candidate and executive information - Excellent communication skills and the professionalism to work comfortably with executives, hiring managers, and candidates from diverse regions and cultures - The ability to prioritize competing deadlines and adapt quickly Nice to have - Experience in crypto, fintech, or another regulated industry Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. items.title: Principal Risk Analyst
items.description: About MoonPay MoonPay is for builders with something to prove. This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. 30M+ customers and 500+ ecosystem partners run on us. Licensed in the U.S. Regulated across the UK, EU, Canada, and Australia. AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters. You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together. The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building for what's next, for humans and agents. Recent recognition: Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 . 2nd in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100 The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. Please know that this list is indicative, and that we would still love to hear from you even if you feel that you are only a 75% match. Skills can be learned, diversity cannot. As a Principal Risk Analyst, you'll identify, measure, and mitigate the risks that come with operating a crypto payments business, including counterparty exposure, liquidity and market risk, and the technical risks unique to blockchain rails. You'll work with Product, Engineering, Compliance, Treasury, and Operations to make sure we can grow quickly without taking risks we don't understand. What You'll Do Review & challenge risk assessment across our payment flows, including on-ramps, off-ramps, card and bank funding, stablecoin settlement, and cross-border transfers. Assess and monitor counterparty risk across liquidity providers, exchanges, custodians, banking partners, payment processors, and blockchain infrastructure vendors. Evaluate exposure from cross-chain bridges, DEX swaps, and smart contract interactions, including protocol risk, liquidity depth, slippage, and settlement failure. Review & challenge risks related to crypto trading, including price slippage, execution latency, and hedging liquidity across venues. Work with Treasury on market, liquidity, and FX risk, including hedging strategy, inventory and float management, and stablecoin de-peg scenarios. Provide an independent review of new product proposals, collaborating early with Product and Engineering, ensuring all risks are identified and controls are integrated from inception, and recommending approval with or without conditions. Review business continuity testing and business impact analyses to ensure operational resilience and preparedness for disruptions. Develop, maintain, and evolve the risk framework, with a strong focus on defining and embedding Risk Appetite Statements and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), alongside risk registers, limits, and escalation procedures. Review technology and information security risks across core systems, infrastructure, and third-party integrations to ensure robust safeguards and data protection. Prepare risk reporting for senior leadership, the board, auditors, and partners Conduct third-party risk assessments and continuous monitoring for critical vendors, service providers, and partners. What You'll Bring Experience 5-10 years in risk management at a payments company, fintech, exchange, bank, or crypto firm. Hands-on experience with credit/counterparty, operational, or market risk in a regulated or high-growth environment. Strong quantitative and analytical skills. You are comfortable building dashboards and models from raw data. Crypto payments knowledge (essential) A deep understanding of how crypto payments work end to end: fiat-to-crypto and crypto-to-fiat flows, crypto swaps, stablecoin settlement, merchant and card acquiring, Working knowledge of blockchain fundamentals: consensus, finality, confirmations, reorgs, gas and fees, wallets, and key management. Understanding of cross-chain bridges and their trust and security models, plus the history of bridge exploits. Understanding of swaps, DEXs and AMMs, liquidity pools, slippage, MEV, and aggregator routing. Knowledge of hedging approaches in crypto, such as spot, perpetuals, futures, options, and stablecoin basis risk. Familiarity with stablecoin mechanics and reserve and de-peg risk, and with smart contract risk and audits. Experience with blockchain analytics tools (e.g., Chainalysis, TRM, Elliptic) and on-chain data exploration. Core skills Excellent judgment under uncertainty. You can make a call with incomplete information and explain your reasoning. Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to translate technical risk into business impact for non-specialists. A collaborative approach: you can say "no" or "yes, with conditions" without becoming a blocker. Nice to Have A professional risk certification (FRM, PRM, CAMS) or a quantitative degree. Experience in DeFi or familiarity with writing or reading simple smart contract logic. Prior experience building a risk function at a scaling company. Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. Please know that this list is indicative, and that we would still love to hear from you even if you feel that you are only a 75% match. Skills can be learned, diversity cannot. items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is seeking a strategic Go-To-Market Recruiter specializing in Applied AI to join our GTM recruiting organization. In this role, you'll focus specifically on building and scaling our Applied AI team - the Pre-Sales architects and technical advisors who help large enterprises successfully integrate and deploy Claude. Working within our broader GTM recruiting team, you'll drive full-cycle recruiting for these critical customer-facing technical roles that bridge our cutting-edge AI technology with real-world business applications. This specialized role requires deep technical recruiting expertise combined with a strong understanding of enterprise SaaS and AI landscapes. You'll collaborate closely with GTM recruiting colleagues while developing targeted strategies for the unique talent needs of our Applied AI organization. You'll help shape how enterprises work with AI systems by building teams that directly influence the safe and beneficial deployment of Claude across industries. Key responsibilities Lead end-to-end recruiting for Applied AI team roles, including Solutions Architects, Pre-Sales Engineers, front-line managers and other customer-facing technical positions Partner with Applied AI leadership and GTM recruiting colleagues to develop comprehensive hiring strategies that align with overall GTM objectives Execute sophisticated sourcing strategies to identify candidates with rare combinations of technical depth, customer empathy, and business acumen Create exceptional candidate experiences that showcase Anthropic's mission and the unique opportunity to shape enterprise AI adoption Build pipelines of talent with expertise in LLMs, cloud architecture, enterprise software integration, and technical consulting Collaborate with GTM recruiting team members to share best practices, market insights, and cross-functional candidate leads Leverage Claude and other AI tools to enhance recruiting efficiency while maintaining high-touch, personalized engagement Provide data-driven insights on compensation trends and talent availability specific to the Applied AI market Minimum qualifications Excel at recruiting for customer-facing technical roles that require both deep technical knowledge and exceptional communication skills Understand the technical requirements of roles working with LLMs, APIs, cloud architectures, and enterprise system integration Thrive in collaborative environments, working seamlessly with GTM recruiting colleagues while managing specialized searches Can effectively assess candidates' abilities to translate complex technical concepts for diverse stakeholders Have a track record of building trusted advisor relationships with technical hiring managers Are passionate about using AI to transform recruiting practices while maintaining a human-centered approach Preferred qualifications Have 5+ years of technical or technical sales recruiting experience, ideally within GTM organizations at enterprise software or AI/ML companies Direct experience recruiting for pre-sales/solutions engineering roles in the AI/ML space Demonstrated success working within GTM recruiting organizations during periods of hypergrowth Expertise in developing specialized recruiting practices within broader team structures Familiarity with the challenges of deploying AI systems in enterprise environments Experience collaborating across recruiting teams to share resources and best practices A technical background or successful track record recruiting for highly specialized technical positions The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $175,000 — $240,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. That’s why we offer early employees stock options as part of their compensation package. - Extraordinary team; we favor ambitious, smart people striving for outsized impact. You’ll work on the state of the art surrounded by people with extraordinary skills and positive attitudes. - We offer competitive compensation and stock options. We are open to candidates of varying seniority. items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world’s longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. We’re looking for a Full Stack Engineer to join a small, dedicated growth and experimentation team within Krak, focused on accelerating acquisition, activation, engagement and trading activity across the Krak app. This is a frontend-leaning full-stack role: the majority of your work will be in React Native, supported by enough backend capability to take an experiment from idea to live without waiting on another team. Rather than executing against a rigid roadmap, you’ll work closely with Product on a continuous pipeline of fast, lightweight experiments, owning each one from hypothesis through implementation, launch, measurement and iteration. The mandate is simple: find the highest-leverage opportunities to grow users and revenue, prove what works, and scale the winners – with direct, measurable impact on how millions of customers discover and use Kraken’s products. The opportunity - Build and ship consumer-facing features quickly in React Native and TypeScript, favouring small, high-velocity experiments over long-running projects. - Own experiments end-to-end – hypothesis, design, build, launch, measurement and iteration – using platforms such as Statsig to test globally or within specific markets. - Improve onboarding, activation and feature discovery to drive conversion, engagement and trading revenue, iterating rapidly on features that are already live. - Build viral acquisition features and value-add growth features on top of Krak’s existing product offering. - Contribute to backend services and APIs wherever an experiment requires it, so you can ship across the stack without being blocked. Our backend is primarily Rust; prior Rust experience is not expected, but enthusiasm for picking it up is. - Read your own results, including trade-offs between conversion gains and other metrics, and decide whether to scale, iterate or kill – driving technical decisions autonomously amid evolving priorities and limited upfront planning. What you bring - 3+ years of software development experience building and shipping large-scale, consumer-facing applications. Strong, hands-on React and React Native experience is essential. - Demonstrated experience running growth experiments at consumer-facing businesses, with measurable impact on conversion, activation, retention or revenue. This is a consumer growth role, so B2B or platform-only backgrounds are not a fit. - Working backend proficiency: you can design and implement services and APIs yourself. We care about backend fundamentals rather than any particular language, and you should be open to working in Rust. - Strong JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals, with hands-on experience across APIs, WebSockets and real-time systems, mobile performance, testing, and modern development workflows. - Practical experience designing, running and analysing A/B tests – feature flags, statistical significance, product analytics, funnel and cohort data – with the judgement to act decisively on what the results show. - End-to-end ownership of product features and a strong product engineering mindset, with the initiative and adaptability to operate with minimal direction amid ambiguity and frequently changing priorities. Nice to haves - Customer-facing product experience within fintech, digital banking, payments, trading or crypto. - Hands-on experience with Statsig or a comparable experimentation platform, including regional and global rollouts. - Rust experience, given our backend stack. - SQL and self-serve analytics, so you can pull and interrogate your own data. - AI fluency. Familiarity with how AI tools and patterns have fundamentally shifted your development workflow and problem-solving approach. - Native mobile development (iOS/Android), distributed systems or microservices, or engineering within a hyperscaling consumer technology organisation. Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto. We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. If you’re ready to shape the future of AI in the public sector and be a founding member of our team, we’d love to hear from you. Develop and maintain full-stack components that integrate with AI models, focusing on building responsive UIs and reliable backend APIs. Assist in deploying and monitoring applications within cloud environments, ensuring basic system stability and security. Help build and refine reusable features that support diverse international client use cases. Work within a multi-disciplinary team of design, product, and data specialists to build robust features that follow established technical architectures. Experience building and deploying web applications with a good understanding of cloud fundamentals and scalable coding practices. A self-starting approach to navigate ambiguous requirements and deliver reliable software. Experience building solutions with LLMs Nice to haves: Proficient in Arabic Experience working cross functionally with operations PLEASE NOTE: Our policy requires a 90-day waiting period before reconsidering candidates for the same role. items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Legal team helps advance our mission by tackling novel legal issues in AI. Our team brings together professionals across technology, privacy, intellectual property, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation. Our regulatory compliance work turns legal requirements into practical programs that support responsible AI development and deployment. About the Role As a Legal Program Manager, you will independently manage assigned programs and workstreams across Legal priorities, with a focus on emerging user risk. Your portfolio may include sensitive user escalations, intake and response workflows, and improvements informed by recurring issues, with the mix evolving alongside team needs. You will partner with counsel, senior legal program managers, and technical and business teams to establish priorities and scope, then drive day-to-day execution. You’ll organize information, coordinate partners, and move open questions toward decisions. As you develop expertise, you’ll take on more ambiguous projects and build repeatable processes that help teams work more effectively. This full-time role is based in San Francisco, CA, or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Independently manage assigned legal programs and workstreams: define plans, owners, milestones, and dependencies within agreed scope, anticipate blockers, and drive execution. - Translate counsel’s and specialist teams’ guidance into repeatable workflows, playbooks, and documentation. Depending on your portfolio, this may include intake, sensitive user escalations, information gathering, and response coordination. - Build strong partnerships across Legal, Product, Safety, User Operations, Policy, and other teams to clarify ownership, coordinate handoffs, and drive commitments through completion. - Clarify open questions, gather and verify information, synthesize partner input, and bring recommendations and tradeoffs to the appropriate decision-makers. Escalate decisions that require changes to priorities, scope, or resources. - Maintain a reliable source of truth for matters, source documents, owners, deadlines, decisions, and actions. Provide concise reporting on progress, blockers, and decisions needed. - Identify recurring issues and execution gaps, propose practical improvements, and lead agreed changes through implementation and adoption. Use tools and automation thoughtfully, verify outputs, and assess improvements in quality, timeliness, and partner effort. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have demonstrated experience independently managing programs or projects from planning through delivery in legal operations, business operations, compliance, policy, investigations, or a related field. - Have experience coordinating work across teams, maintaining reliable records, and driving open questions and actions to resolution. Experience working with an in-house legal team or in a technology environment is a plus. - Have improved a recurring workflow, documented the change, and helped others adopt it. You can explain what improved and how you assessed the result. - Take ownership of execution, set and achieve milestones, anticipate dependencies, and follow through without frequent direction. - Bring strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills. Exercise sound judgment under pressure, adapt to changing priorities, and know when to proceed independently or seek guidance. - Handle sensitive information and difficult subject matter with discretion and care, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and recognize when counsel or specialist input is needed. - Are resourceful and hands-on, with enthusiasm for AI technology and the ability to learn unfamiliar subject areas, use AI tools thoughtfully, and verify their outputs. - Bring familiarity with user safety, legal escalations, preservation, incident response, or operational data as a plus. Our mission is to bridge traditional commerce with Web3, enabling seamless checkout and funding experiences whether users pay via fiat (cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay) or crypto (self-custodial wallets, Coinbase retail accounts, and stablecoins). You will drive the product roadmap for core offerings including our Payment Acceptance API, OAuth deep-linking integrations, and headless Onramp APIs. You will play a pivotal role in expanding global merchant adoption and setting the benchmark for stablecoin and digital asset payments. Global Regulatory & Licensing Acumen: Solid familiarity with cross-border payment regulations, fintech compliance, and international licensing frameworks across major regions such as the US, EU, and LatAm. items.title: Public Policy, Strategic Advisory
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We’re hiring a strategic advisor to join the Strategic Advisory team within Policy Advocacy, part of Anthropic’s Public Policy team. This is an individual contributor role at the strategic heart of Anthropic’s policy function — designed for an operator with 8–10+ years of experience who wants to drive clarity on Anthropic’s most consequential policy positions, partner with cross-functional peers, and be deployed as a strategic resource across fast-moving policy work. Policy Advocacy turns Anthropic’s policy priorities into evidence-backed positions, research, campaigns, and partnerships — distinct from government relations and communications, but essential to enabling both. This role is designed to complement our existing Strategic Advisory capacity, which owns the documentation, translation, and deployment of Anthropic’s positions so that external-facing teams can use them. You’ll bring experience and judgment into the room, hold responsibility for a portfolio of strategically important positions, and partner as a peer with leaders across the policy, legal, comms, and product policy functions, working with colleagues on teams across the company on positions and messaging. The ideal candidate is effective across multiple stakeholders even through substantive disagreement, prioritizes closure over deliberation, and organized and process-focused but able to operate in ambiguity. Successful candidates will have experience building structure where none exists, including under unclear ownership and shifting priorities. We prize doers willing to do the work directly, no matter how small or large. Strategic and systems thinkers that understand how individual positions and engagements fit together across the broader policy landscape are encouraged to apply. Examples of work in this role might include producing a position package end-to-end: pressure-testing the position with internal SMEs (policy, legal, research), identifying and closing gaps, and producing the full set of deployable materials. Translating new technical research or policy analysis into policy-ready materials on short timelines for use by federal, state, and international affairs teams. Building and running a structured process to resolve a contested position and documenting the outcome. Leading the cross-functional policy strategy for a major launch, including alignment across policy, legal, comms, and research on external narrative, broader policy implications, and rapid-response plans. Standing up a cross-functional working group on an emerging platform or corporate issue, including scoping the problem, driving alignment across teams, producing a written strategy, and standing up the workstream. Distilling Anthropic’s approach to a complex or evolving issue into a deployable narrative, and integrating the output into the canon. This role offers a rare opportunity to shape Anthropic’s policy voice across the most consequential debates in AI governance, while operating with the pace, pragmatism, and service orientation of a top-tier public affairs function. Key responsibilities Own a portfolio of Anthropic’s highest-priority policy positions, including position papers, FAQs, talking points, and fact sheets — managing versions, intended audiences, strategic relevance, and internal access. Drive organizational consensus on contested technical policy positions — working with subject matter experts across federal affairs, state affairs, international affairs, national security, legal, comms, and research — moderating dissent, calling the question, and closing the loop on documented positions. Develop and test message framings with internal and external audiences, iterating quickly and bringing rigor to what lands and why. Translate technical research, model capability, and scientific content into policy-ready language for federal, state, and international policymakers, their staff, and legislators. Serve federal, state, and international affairs teams as an internal senior advisor — improving their processes, standing up shared material libraries, and building the collateral and strategies they need to be effective in their markets. Drive complex, cross-functional policy projects to resolution when no single team is set up to own them end to end — including model launch policy strategy, narrative coordination on contested issues, and working groups on emerging topics. Stand up rapid-response playbooks when time-sensitive events require Anthropic to move in days rather than weeks, coordinating across legal, research, and external affairs. Partner with policy communications to ensure message and voice consistency across Anthropic’s policy surface area. Anticipate emerging issues, proactively work with internal experts to develop Anthropic’s perspective, and make sure we have the materials we need before external pressure emerges. Minimum qualifications Have direct experience with message development and testing for policy, advocacy, or communications audiences. Have experience translating technical material (scientific, engineering, or deeply technical policy) for non-expert decision-makers. Are comfortable operating at breadth across multiple policy issue areas simultaneously, and can develop fluency in new ones quickly. Interest in and some experience with technology policy is important; deep AI policy expertise is a plus, not a prerequisite. Have experience building or running rapid-response processes, crisis playbooks, or signature programs in fast-moving environments. Can serve internal clients — federal, state, and international affairs colleagues — without needing to own external relationships yourself. You find that service posture energizing, not limiting. Preferred qualifications Have 8–10+ years of professional experience in corporate public affairs, management consulting, government relations, policy or political campaigns, think tanks, or similar fast-paced, cross-functional environments. Experience in technology, financial services, energy, pharma, or other heavily regulated industries. Demonstrated ability to anticipate emerging issues and develop organizational perspectives proactively. Experience designing and running a signature program or flagship campaign end-to-end. Experience translating topics to policy-relevant audiences through communications, visual storytelling, marketing, or advocacy. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $265,000 — $295,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Threat Analyst
items.description: 📢 Join Novibet as a Threat Analyst ! Are you ready to take on a key role in a dynamic, fast-growing company? If you have a passion for investigating attacker behavior, analyzing logs, and turning complex signals into meaningful intelligence, this role is for you. Who We Are Founded in 2010, Novibet is an established global GameTech company operating in Europe, the Americas, and other international markets (Greece, Brazil, Mexico, Malta, Ireland, Cyprus, Chile, Finland and New Zealand), with hubs in Greece, Malta, Brazil, and Mexico and more than 1,400 employees worldwide. We are driven by technology and innovation, continuously evolving our proprietary platform to deliver seamless and engaging online entertainment experiences to our growing customer base. Why Novibet At Novibet, you’ll be empowered to take on meaningful challenges, develop your skills and contribute ideas that make a difference. Certified as a Great Place to Work® several years in a row, in Greece, Malta and Brazil, we are a global team, united by a culture of trust, inclusion and shared learning. Join us and become part of a global team where collaboration, innovation and continuous growth drive everything we do. What you will work on We are looking for a Threat Analyst to join and strengthen the Novibet Cybersecurity Team. In this role, you will be at the heart of our security operations - detecting threats, investigating incidents, and helping us stay one step ahead of attackers. You will analyze alerts, investigate suspicious activity, and transform security data into actionable insights. items.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Cyber - SF
items.description: About the team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems. About the role You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions. You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground. You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it. This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required. In this role you will: - Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria. - Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review. - Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates. - Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence. - Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt. You might thrive in this role if you: - 5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production software. - Experience protecting production systems through work in security engineering, infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or product engineering. - Experience building and evaluating AI agents for software engineering workflows. - Experience with CI/CD pipelines and practices that maintain code quality, reliability, and security. - Ability to navigate unfamiliar codebases and contribute maintainable, production-quality changes. - Ability to communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to engineering teams and senior security stakeholders. Additional experience Cybersecurity spans many disciplines, and while we’re primarily looking for strong engineering generalists, we’d love to hear about deeper experience in any of the following areas: - Security curiosity and experimentation: You read CVE write-ups because you want to understand how things break. You may have built an agent honeypot to test a hypothesis—or prove a point—and enjoy turning a security question into a hands-on experiment. - Security community engagement: You enjoy exchanging ideas with defenders, whether that’s discussing security strategy with a CISO at Black Hat or comparing technical approaches with frontline practitioners. - Application security: You’ve written CodeQL queries or Semgrep rules, built fuzzing harnesses, or discovered and responsibly disclosed vulnerabilities. - Automated remediation: CI/CD is your happy place. You’ve built tooling that turns security findings into tested patches, dependency upgrades, or configuration changes across large codebases. - Detection engineering: You’ve written and deployed detections using Sigma, YARA, Splunk, or KQL and tested them against attacker behavior. - Cloud and identity security: You’ve designed cloud IAM architectures and investigated abuse of workload identities, role hierarchies, or cross-account trust. - Security research: You’ve reverse-engineered malware, developed exploit reproductions, or contributed to vulnerability research. - Agent security: You’ve tested agents for prompt injection, tool misuse, or credential exposure and built defenses against them. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. items.title: Customer Experience Team Lead, RHM Executive Office
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. Robinhood’s Customer Experience team plays a critical role in Democratizing Finance for All. Our customer experience team supports customers across a wide range of account needs, delivering timely, accurate, and empathetic support across multiple channels. As a Customer Experience Team Lead within the Executive Office, you will serve as a technical leader and subject matter expert, helping our team deliver accurate, timely, and thoughtful resolutions to complex customer concerns. You will provide hands-on coaching, strengthen investigative and problem-solving capabilities, and support consistent execution of our quality and regulatory standards. You’ll partner closely with the Customer Experience Manager to drive operational excellence, manage case priorities, and identify opportunities to improve processes and customer outcomes. This role requires strong judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to navigate sensitive situations while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Schedule & Work Environment This role is based in our Westlake, TX office or Denver, CO, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days a week. The team operates on a 7:00am - 10:00pm EST schedule . Employees will work either five 8-hour shifts or four 10-hour shifts per week, depending on business needs. Specific schedules will be determined after hire. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Serve as a technical subject matter expert, providing guidance and coaching on complex customer complaints, investigations, and escalations. Develop team capabilities through hands-on coaching, case reviews, knowledge sharing, and actionable feedback that strengthens quality, judgment, and resolution effectiveness. Support daily operations by monitoring case queues, prioritizing time-sensitive matters, and ensuring cases are assigned, progressed, and resolved within established service-level and regulatory timelines. Provide guidance on sensitive or high-risk customer situations, partnering with Compliance, Legal, and other internal teams to support appropriate resolution. Monitor case quality, productivity, and operational trends, identifying opportunities to improve team performance, processes, and the customer experience. Partner with the Customer Experience Manager to reinforce operational standards, drive accountability, and support continuous improvement initiatives. Lead by example by directly managing complex customer cases and supporting the team during periods of increased volume or operational need. What you bring Active FINRA Series 7, Series 63, Series 9/10 OR Series 24 preferred. Ability to obtain Series 3 within 120 days) Experience handling complex customer concerns, escalations, or complaints within a financial services or regulated environment. Strong technical coaching and leadership skills, with the ability to develop others through feedback, guidance, and knowledge sharing. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate clearly and professionally in sensitive or high-stakes situations. Strong investigative, analytical, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail. Sound judgment and the ability to balance customer outcomes, regulatory requirements, and business priorities. items.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Financial Services- NYC
items.description: About the team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with banks, asset managers, insurers, and private capital firms to deploy production-grade AI systems in high-stakes financial environments. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development, embedding deeply with customers to translate frontier model capabilities into reliable, auditable systems that create measurable business impact. Our work turns early deployments into repeatable solution patterns, operating standards, and evaluation practices that scale across regulated financial institutions. About the role We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to lead end-to-end deployments of OpenAI’s models inside financial services organizations where correctness, latency, explainability, and control matter. You will work with customers who are experts in investment banking, trading, risk, compliance, underwriting, research, operations, or investment decision-making, translating complex workflows, data constraints, and regulatory requirements into production systems. You will measure success through production adoption, workflow efficiency, risk reduction, revenue impact, and evaluation-driven feedback loops that inform product, model, and GTM strategy. You’ll work closely with Product, Research, GTM, Security, Legal, and GRC to deliver systems that meet enterprise standards for governance, auditability, and operational resilience. You will also play a central role in shaping OpenAI’s Financial Services offering — identifying high-value use cases, defining solution patterns, and building the first repeatable deployments that scale across institutions. Learn more about some of our work with financial institutions https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-financial-services/. This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% may be required. In this role, you will: - Design and ship production AI systems around models, owning integrations, data flows, reliability, observability, and on-call readiness across financial workflows. - Lead discovery and scoping from pre-sales through post-production, translating ambiguous business problems into hypothesis-driven problem framing, system requirements, and delivery plans with measurable outcomes. - Define and enforce launch criteria for regulated financial environments, including controls, audit artifacts, evaluation benchmarks, and acceptance thresholds tied to risk and performance. - Build in sensitive data environments where access controls, data lineage, explainability, and failure modes shape architecture and operating procedures. - Run evaluation loops that measure model and system quality against workflow-specific financial benchmarks (e.g., accuracy, latency, coverage, false positives) and use results to drive iteration. - Own delivery state across multiple workstreams, making trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality to protect production outcomes. - Distill deployment learnings into hardened primitives, reference architectures, playbooks, and tooling that scale across financial institutions. - Surface field feedback that informs model behavior, product capabilities, and platform gaps in real-world financial use cases. You might thrive in this role if you: - Bring 5+ years of software engineering, ML engineering, or technical deployment experience with customer-facing ownership in financial services or adjacent regulated industries. - Have owned complex AI or data-driven systems end-to-end, from scoping through production adoption, in environments where errors carry real financial or regulatory consequences. - Have experience with financial workflows such as research, trading, risk, compliance, underwriting, operations, or investment processes, and understand how incentives and controls shape adoption. - Write and review production-grade code across backend and frontend systems using Python, JavaScript, or comparable stacks. - Have deployed systems powered by LLMs or generative models and understand how model behavior, evaluation, and guardrails affect user trust and business outcomes. - Communicate clearly across engineering, product, risk, compliance, and executive stakeholders, translating technical trade-offs into decision quality and risk posture. - Apply systems thinking with high execution standards, turning incidents, escalations, and failures into improved operating standards and repeatable deployment patterns. - Stay calm and decisive when delivery is urgent, ambiguous, and high-stakes. items.title: International Equity Accounting and Reporting
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are looking for an experienced accountant to own Equity Accounting and Reporting at Anthropic, based in San Francisco. You will be the one owner of equity accounting numbers across US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP in every jurisdiction where we have employees holding equity: expense booking by entity, intercompany recharge booking, current and deferred tax on equity, and the equity footnote and local statutory disclosures, prepared once and reused. You will own equity reporting data from Shareworks, our equity administration platform, through to the ledgers, while staying hands-on: preparing and reviewing close materials, owning your own accounts, and serving as the first escalation point for the judgment calls in your domain. Share-based compensation (SBC) is one of the most cross-functional areas of our reporting. Grants, vesting, exercises and the events that follow each carry requirements for US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP expense, pushdown and recharge postings, tax provisioning, payroll withholding, transfer pricing and statutory disclosure, and those needs are met across Equity Administration, Equity Reporting, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Transfer Pricing and Global Payroll from a single set of award-level records. This is a build role: you will take the open workstreams from manual to automated, work with Finance Systems and Shareworks to build the reports each stage needs, finalize the policies and agreements that sit behind recharges, and bring the end-to-end process to a scalable, efficient and fully compliant close. We are looking for someone who has owned equity accounting in a growing global organization before and wants to do it again at one of the most important companies in the world. Key responsibilities Close ownership Own the equity portfolio through month-end and quarter-end close: US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP equity expense, pushed down and booked by entity, including reconciliations, journal entries and variance commentary Own intercompany recharge booking: invoicing, settlement, Treasury communication and the foreign exchange (FX) that follows Own current and deferred tax on equity by entity and in local currency, including the IFRS deferred tax mark to the share price and windfalls or shortfalls through the tax provision Ensure every close deliverable is audit-ready, with clear documentation of positions and supporting evidence Technical accounting and policy Write, own and maintain the accounting policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for equity across US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP: grant-date fair value and expense schedules, recharge basis by entity, mobility apportionment, and the treatment of cancellations, modifications and one-off events Partner closely with Tax to close every open policy position and execute the recharge agreements that depend on them Research the tax and accounting rules for each new jurisdiction entered and categorize it under our framework before the first grant lands there Own the equity footnote and local statutory disclosures for all entities, including the award rollforward for each period with internal transfers, and the external audit responses that support them Controls Design and operate Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controls across equity expense, recharges and deferred tax; review control evidence and own timely remediation of any gaps Establish completeness and cut-off controls so that the same award, the same entity, the same event dates and the same FX rate flow from Shareworks to every ledger, report and return Systems and automation Anticipate changes in reporting needs and work with Finance Systems and Shareworks to build them: IFRS expense and deferred tax reports in local currency at Workday rates, mobility snapshots driving expense apportionment, corporate tax apportionment rules, and exercise and disclosure reports with mobility detail Automate the monthly pushdown and recharge postings and the reconciliation of deferred tax to expense reports, replacing manual work Document workflows and controls in a way that supports knowledge transfer, audit evidence and scale Cross-functional partnership Partner with Equity Administration, Equity Reporting, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Transfer Pricing and Global Payroll so each stage of an award is handled from every statutory and reporting perspective and every stakeholder has the data they need Record in the local books (secondary ledgers) the local SBC expense and recharges that feed the cost base for transfer pricing Translate complex equity accounting into plain language for non-finance stakeholders Equity events Lead the cross-functional, cross-jurisdictional review of one-off equity events such as tender offers and share repurchases, covering the accounting, the deduction, payroll withholding, Treasury and the resulting disclosures Coordinate with Tax and advisers on open conclusions, such as the apportionment logic for corporation tax versus payroll tax, so report configurations are right before they are built, manual rework is minimized and the data serves every purpose it is built for Minimum qualifications Certified Public Accountant (CPA) or equivalent professional accounting qualification Deep, hands-on experience with stock-based compensation under Accounting Standards Codification Topic 718 (ASC 718), IFRS 2 and local GAAP, including equity roll-forwards and reconciliation to an equity administration platform Experience with the tax accounting for equity: current and deferred tax by entity, mobility apportionment, and windfalls and shortfalls through the provision Experience owning a portfolio of accounts through close in a public company or pre-initial public offering (IPO) environment, including designing and operating SOX controls Experience writing and maintaining accounting policies and SOPs, and being accountable for how they are applied Ability to structure ambiguous problems, reach defensible conclusions and document them clearly Clear written and verbal communication with non-accounting partners Preferred qualifications Progressive accounting experience that combines Big 4 audit with time at a high-growth or startup company A clear point of view on how artificial intelligence (AI) tools can eliminate low-value accounting work, and a track record of putting it into practice A project management qualification or experience running cross-functional workstreams The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: Software is eating the world, but AI is eating software. We live in unprecedented times – AI has the potential to exponentially augment human intelligence. Every person will have a personal tutor, coach, assistant, personal shopper, travel guide, and therapist throughout life. As the world adjusts to this new reality, leading platform companies are scrambling to build LLMs at billion scale, while large enterprises figure out how to add it to their products. At Scale, our products include the Generative AI Data Engine, SGP, Donovan, and others that power the most advanced LLMs and generative models in the world through world-class RLHF, human data generation, model evaluation, safety, and alignment. The data we are producing is some of the most important work for how humanity will interact with AI. At the foundation of these products is the Platform Engineering team. In this role, you will redefine how engineers develop, build, test, and deploy software at Scale using AI development tools in addition to traditional practices. You’ll also get widespread exposure to the forefront of the AI race as Scale sees it in enterprises, startups, governments, and large tech companies. You will: Define next-generation AI development tooling and frameworks using products like Cursor, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and MS Copilot, as well as in-house custom-built solutions. Drive the architecture, design, and implementation of our local development process, build, test, continuous integration, and continuous delivery systems, working closely with stakeholders and internal customers to understand and refine requirements. Directly mentor software engineers ranging from new grads to experienced engineers. Proactively identify opportunities and drive improvements to software development practices, processes, tools, and languages. Present technical information to teams and stakeholders, providing guidance and insight on development processes and technologies. Ideally you’d have: 8+ years of full-time engineering experience, post-graduation, with experience in build, test, or CI/CD systems. Extensive experience defining and evangelizing best-practices for AI development tools, including cost guardrails, security frameworks, and hosting knowledge-sharing sessions, among others. Extensive experience in software development and a deep understanding of distributed systems and public cloud platforms (AWS preferred). Experience configuring, testing, and enabling MCP servers, AI agents, and other associated systems. Show a track record of independent ownership of successful engineering projects. Possess excellent communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to translate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. Experience working fluently with standard infrastructure, containerization, and deployment technologies like Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, etc. Experience with modern web frameworks like NodeJS, NextJS, etc. Strong knowledge of software engineering best practices and CI/CD tooling (CircleCI, Helm, ArgoCD). Nice to haves: Experience scaling products at hyper-growth startups. Experience with modern build systems like Bazel, Buck, Pants, etc. Compensation packages at Scale for eligible roles include base salary, equity, and benefits. items.title: Founding Full Stack Software Engineer, Consulting
items.description: About the Team The Consulting team is part of OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. Our goal is to help consulting teams do better work for their clients. We work side by side with design partners to understand how their teams operate, then use what we learn to build for consultants everywhere. Today, we’re bringing OpenAI’s models and products together to accelerate the core work of consulting, from investigating a client’s question to delivering advice they can act on. We’re starting by removing the barriers that keep consultants from using AI in their day-to-day work. We’ll draw on the full range of OpenAI’s capabilities, from ChatGPT Work to newer tools such as Dots and Spaces. Longer term, we want to help firms develop AI-native ways of working. A team could design an engagement around questions it can now afford to explore, test several strategies with its client, and change course as it learns what works. We’re moving quickly, working across OpenAI’s research, product, and engineering teams to turn what we learn with design partners into products consultants everywhere can use. About the Role We’re looking for a full-stack software engineer to build first-party OpenAI products for consulting. You’ll own features end to end, from the frontend interfaces consultants use to the backend services and integrations that power them. You’ll work closely with our consulting design partners and with colleagues across product, design, research, and engineering at OpenAI. Together, you’ll turn what you learn from individual engagement teams into products we can distribute broadly. Success will ultimately be defined by adoption and the value generated for consulting firms. In this role, you will: - Work directly with our design partners. Sit with consultants and engagement leaders, observe how they work, and identify problems worth solving across firms. - Design and prototype experiences that help consultants do an important part of their job better from day one. - Build across the stack, from the user interface to the services and APIs that connect OpenAI’s models with the tools consultants use. - Build for firms with different methods and working environments while protecting the confidential information clients entrust to them. - Evaluate what you build with design partners and researchers. Use real assignments to see where it improves the work and what still needs to change. - Ship the product to consulting teams broadly and own its rollout and reliability. Use feedback and production data to guide improvements after launch. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have shipped and operated a substantial product, with hands-on ownership across frontend and backend systems. - Have strong product and interface instincts, especially when people need to understand, question, or correct what software produces. - Enjoy working directly with users and can tell when one customer’s request points to a problem many people share. - Can turn an unfamiliar workflow into a working prototype, then make the technical choices it takes to support many teams. - Make thoughtful tradeoffs about quality, speed, and reliability and can explain those choices to colleagues across disciplines. Nice to Have - Firsthand consulting experience combined with hands-on experience building and shipping software. - Building software for research, analysis, collaboration, or other complex professional work. - Developing AI applications and evaluating their usefulness with expert users. - Designing enterprise products that handle sensitive information or fit into different organizations’ ways of working. - Taking a product from its first few users to broad adoption as a founder or early engineer. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm. Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products. Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group. About the Role We are looking for a Software Engineer to join the Guardian team in London. You will design and build production systems that evaluate agent behavior, identify risk, and take appropriate action without creating unnecessary friction for users. This is a hands-on engineering role with substantial technical depth and ownership. You will work across architecture, implementation, evaluation, and operations, taking projects from early exploration through production deployment. The work requires strong engineering fundamentals, sound product judgment, and comfort solving problems where both the requirements and the underlying technology are evolving. You will work closely with alignment researchers to translate emerging research into dependable systems, and with product and engineering teams to make agent safety a foundational capability across OpenAI. This role is based in our London office.
